title: The 10 Best Cordless Random Orbital Sanders
subtitle: Battery-powered 5-inch random orbit sanders ranked from live Amazon data — swirl-free finishes with no cord to drag around.
intro: A cordless random orbital sander trades a little runtime for the freedom to sand a car hood, a stair rail, or a ladder-top window frame without hunting for an outlet. This list covers bare tools for buyers already on a battery platform (DeWalt, Milwaukee, Makita, Craftsman, Metabo HPT) alongside complete kits that include a battery and charger, sorted by what varies most: variable speed, dust collection, and whether it ships ready to use.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Random Orbital Sander Kit (DCW210P1)

specs.dust: Dust bag + DWV010/012 dust collector port

products.verdict: The most complete package on this list. It's the same brushless DCW210B tool below, but sold with a 5.0Ah battery and charger so it's ready to sand out of the box. The variable-speed dial runs 8,000 to 12,000 OPM, and the sander attaches directly to a DEWALT dust collector or the included locking dust bag.
pros: Ships with a 5.0Ah battery and charger, not just the bare tool
Brushless motor with an 8,000–12,000 OPM variable-speed dial
Attaches directly to DWV010/012 dust collectors, not just a bag
cons: The most expensive tool on this list by a wide margin
Overkill if you already own a DEWALT 20V battery

products.name: AVID POWER 20V Cordless Random Orbital Sander Tool 5", 6 Variable Speeds
products.verdict: The budget pick, and the only kit here under $50. It comes with a 20V 2.0Ah battery, a charger, and 30 sandpapers across three grits, so there's nothing else to buy. Six speed settings from 7,000 to 11,000 RPM cover most light sanding jobs around the house.
pros: Only full kit (battery + charger) under $50
6 variable speeds from 7,000 to 11,000 RPM
Ships with 30 sandpapers across 3 grits
cons: Brushed motor, not brushless
Dust bag only — no port for a shop vac hose

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Orbital Sander, Tool Only (DCW210B)

specs.dust: Dust bag + DWV010/012 dust collector port

products.verdict: The best-selling cordless sander on Amazon by a wide margin — nearly 14,000 reviews at 4.7 stars. It's the bare-tool version of the kit above: same brushless motor, same 8,000–12,000 OPM dial, same dust-sealed switch. The obvious buy if you already own a DEWALT 20V battery.
pros: 13,908 reviews at 4.7 stars, the most-reviewed sander in this category
Brushless motor with variable-speed control
Low-profile design gets close to the work surface
cons: Tool only — battery and charger sold separately
Costs almost as much as the full kit once you add a battery

products.name: Milwaukee Electric Tools 2648-20 M18 Random Orbit Sander

pros: 3,591 reviews at 4.7 stars, 600+ bought last month
Powerful motor removes material fast for a cordless sander
Up to 35 minutes of runtime on a 3.0Ah M18 battery

products.name: Makita XOB01Z 18V LXT Lithium-Ion Cordless 5" Random Orbit Sander, Tool Only

Pad brake reduces free-spin for a cleaner finish
Up to 40 minutes of runtime on a single charge

avoid.name: Cordless Random Orbital Sander Compatible for Dew 20V Max, 5-Inch Brushless Orbit Sander with 19000 RPM
avoid.flag: Trademark-dodging brand name and a spec sheet that doesn't add up
avoid.verdict: This listing leans on a name that's designed to be mistaken for DeWalt, and its headline spec is physically out of step with every real brand on this list. Buy a named-brand bare tool instead — CRAFTSMAN's CMCW220B is cheaper and its numbers are honest.
reasons: The brand is "Dew," not DeWalt — a near-miss name that lets the listing ride DeWalt-compatibility searches while dodging Amazon's brand-name trademark checks. It's a pattern worth being suspicious of on any tool listing.

It advertises a 19,000 RPM top speed. Every named-brand sander in this category — DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita, Metabo HPT, CRAFTSMAN — tops out between 11,000 and 12,000 OPM. A 5-inch random-orbit pad spinning 60% faster than the entire category isn't a performance edge; it's an inflated number, and running a pad that fast is more likely to burn a finish and chew through sandpaper than sand better.

The spec sheet lists "21 volts," despite the whole listing being pitched as compatible with 20V Max DeWalt batteries (which run 20V max / 18V nominal). That's an internal inconsistency, the kind that shows up when a spec sheet gets copy-pasted rather than verified against the actual battery platform.

It's a bare tool with no battery included, but that fact doesn't show up clearly in the title the way it does on legitimate bare-tool listings — a buyer comparing this $43 price to a $50 complete kit above may not realize a compatible battery is still a separate purchase.

buyers_guide.q: Bare tool or a complete kit?
buyers_guide.a: If you already own batteries and a charger for a brand — DeWalt, Milwaukee, Makita, RYOBI, CRAFTSMAN, Metabo HPT — buy the bare tool; it's cheaper and adds one more tool to a battery system you already have. If you're starting from scratch, a kit like the AVID POWER or BLACK+DECKER that bundles a battery and charger is the better value than buying a bare tool and a battery separately.

Variable speed lets you slow the pad down for delicate work like veneer or paint prep, where full speed can burn or gouge, and speed it up for fast material removal. A single-speed tool like the CRAFTSMAN or BLACK+DECKER is fine for general use; if you sand a mix of materials, pay for the dial.

buyers_guide.q: How much runtime should I expect?
buyers_guide.a: A cordless random orbital sander typically runs 20 to 40 minutes on a mid-size battery (2.0–3.0Ah), depending on speed and pressure. If you're sanding all day, keep a second battery charging, or consider a corded sander instead — see our corded random orbital sander picks.

A cloth dust bag is convenient but fills fast and lets fine dust through. A tool with a hose port — like the DEWALT, CRAFTSMAN, RYOBI, or Metabo HPT picks here — connects to a shop vac for far better dust collection, which matters more indoors than outside.

Not directly for sanding power. "20V MAX" and "18V" are largely marketing conventions — DeWalt and Craftsman rate their packs at their maximum unloaded voltage (20V), while Makita and Milwaukee use the nominal voltage (18V) for the same class of battery. What matters is staying within one brand's battery platform, not comparing the number on the box across brands.

buyers_guide.q: Is a 5-inch pad standard on cordless sanders too?
buyers_guide.a: Yes. Every sander on this list uses a 5-inch, 8-hole hook-and-loop pad, the same size and hole pattern as corded random orbital sanders, so sandpaper is interchangeable between the two.
